title_en: Ningbo Municipal People's Procuratorate of Zhejiang Province v. Ningbo Libaidai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd., Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong — case of illegal business operations
ruling_gist_en: Where an actor establishes a company for the purpose of illegally operating securities business, exceeds the company's business scope as registered and approved by the administrative department for industry and commerce, and, without approval from the statutory authority, acts as an agent to sell equity (shares) of non-listed joint stock companies to the unspecified public, such conduct constitutes an illegal business act of operating securities business without approval and disrupting the national securities market. If the circumstances are serious, the actor shall be convicted and punished for the crime of illegal business operation.
keywords_en: Criminal; Illegal business operation; First instance; Intermediate People's Court; Zhejiang Province; Legal person; Natural person; Criminal Law; Determination of illegal securities business operation; Determination of unit crime; Supporting plaintiff; Illegal agency sale of non-listed equity; Ultra vires business operation; Deceiving investors; Securities
full_text_en:
Procuratorial Authority of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province v.

Ningbo Libaidai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd., Chen Zongwei,

Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong — dispute over illegal business operation

【Ruling Summary】

Where an actor establishes a company for the purpose of illegally engaging in securities business, exceeds the business scope approved and registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce, and, without approval from the competent authorities, offers to sell equity (shares) of non-listed joint stock limited companies to unspecified members of the public, such conduct constitutes illegal business operation that disrupts the national securities market without authorization. If the circumstances are serious, the actor shall be convicted and punished for the crime of illegal business operation.

Procuratorial Authority: Procuratorial Authority of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province.

Defendant Unit: Ningbo Libaidai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd., domiciled at Kaiming Street, Haishu District, Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province.

Defendant: Chen Zongwei, male, 42 years old, formerly General Manager of Ningbo Libaidai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd.

Defendant: Wang Wenze, male, 31 years old, formerly Chairman of the Board of Ningbo Libaidai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd.

Defendant: Zheng Chunzhong, male, 27 years old, formerly Deputy General Manager of Ningbo Libaidai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd.

The Procuratorial Authority of Ningbo City, Zhejiang Province, initiated a public prosecution against the defendant unit Ningbo Libaidai Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Libaidai Company") and the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong for the crime of illegal business operation, and submitted the case to the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province for trial.

The indictment alleged: During their respective tenures as General Manager, Chairman of the Board, and Deputy General Manager of the defendant unit Libaidai Company, the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, starting from December 2003, instructed the company's salespersons to promote shares of non-listed joint stock limited companies and falsely claimed that the promoted original shares and stocks would be listed shortly, thereby illegally engaging in the sale of shares of non-listed joint stock limited companies. By the end of November 2004, Libaidai Company had sold 229,000 shares of Shaanxi Sunshine Bioengineering Co., Ltd. to 30 persons including Chen Jianhong; sold 218,000 shares of Western Century Software Co., Ltd. to 39 persons including Chen Yuqin; sold 908,500 shares of Xi'an Shengwei Technology Industry Co., Ltd. to 87 persons including Shao Haiping; and sold 533,000 shares of Shaanxi Zhongke Aerospace Agricultural Development Co., Ltd. to 60 persons including Wang Baolan. The total number of shares of non-listed joint stock limited companies sold reached 1,888,500 shares, and the total sales amount exceeded RMB 6.57 million. Libaidai Company, for the purpose of seeking illegal profits, engaged in securities business without approval from the relevant competent state authorities, and its conduct constituted the crime of illegal business operation, which was a unit crime. Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, as the directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible persons for the unit crime of Libaidai Company, also committed the crime of illegal business operation. The court was requested to impose punishment according to law.

The defendant unit Libaidai Company, the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, and their defense counsels all argued that: The defendant unit and the three defendants were engaged in normal agency transfer business of property rights (equity), not securities business; engaging in the transfer of equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies does not equate to illegal securities business. Non-listed joint stock limited companies also have the right to transfer equity according to law and can be listed on lawfully established property rights trading institutions. After being authorized, the defendant unit disclosed information and promoted the transfer of equity of the involved non-listed joint stock limited companies, which was a lawful business activity. After being penalized, the defendant unit, with the approval of the administrative department for industry and commerce, added "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" to its business scope and continued to engage in equity agency transfer business, based on reliance on the administrative department for industry and commerce. In summary, the conduct of the defendant unit and the three defendants did not constitute the crime of illegal business operation, and the charges in the indictment were unfounded.

The Ningbo Intermediate People's Court found at first instance:

In December 2003, the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, for the purpose of engaging in the agency sale of shares of non-listed joint stock limited companies, established the defendant unit Libaidai Company by registration. Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong served as General Manager, Chairman of the Board, and Deputy General Manager, respectively. The business scope of the company, as approved and registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce, was: investment planning and consulting for industrial projects, accounting business consulting, enterprise management consulting, enterprise joint-stock reform, and enterprise restructuring planning and consulting.

After the establishment of the defendant unit Libaidai Company, the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, through the Nanjing Congtai Investment Management Co., Ltd., established by Taiwanese individuals Zhou Wenlong, Xiao Yuancai, and others, acted as agents to sell shares of four non-listed joint stock limited companies established in Shaanxi Province, namely, Shaanxi Sunshine Bioengineering Co., Ltd., Western Century Software Co., Ltd., Xi'an Shengwei Technology Industry Co., Ltd., and Shaanxi Zhongke Aerospace Agricultural Development Co., Ltd., and negotiated with Nanjing Congtai Investment Management Co., Ltd. to determine the external sales price per share and the internal transfer price. The three defendants falsely claimed to the public that the shares of the aforementioned non-listed joint stock limited companies would be listed shortly and could yield high returns from original shares, and instructed the company's salespersons to promote and sell the shares of the aforementioned non-listed joint stock limited companies to unspecified members of the public. On March 30, 2004, the Ningbo Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, on the grounds that the company's conduct exceeded its approved and registered business scope, issued a decision ordering corrective action and imposing a fine of RMB 10,000. In April of the same year, after approval, the company added "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" to its business scope and continued to act as an agent for the sale of shares of the aforementioned non-listed joint stock limited companies.

By the end of November 2004, under the control of the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, the defendant unit Libaidai Company sold 229,000 shares of Shaanxi Sunshine Bioengineering Co., Ltd. to 30 persons including Chen Jianhong at RMB 3.2 per share; sold 218,000 shares of Western Century Software Co., Ltd. to 39 persons including Chen Yuqin at RMB 3 per share; sold 908,500 shares of Xi'an Shengwei Technology Industry Co., Ltd. to 87 persons including Shao Haiping at RMB 3.9 to 4 per share; and sold 533,000 shares of Shaanxi Zhongke Aerospace Agricultural Development Co., Ltd. to 60 persons including Wang Baolan at RMB 3 to 3.2 per share. The total sales amount of the above shares exceeded RMB 6.57 million, and the defendant unit Libaidai Company gained illegal profits of more than RMB 2.4 million.

The defendant unit Libaidai Company did not engage in any other business after its establishment.

The above facts were confirmed by the testimonies of more than 100 share-purchasing investors including Jin Jianzhou, and employees of the defendant unit Libaidai Company such as Chen Yaping; the defendant unit's detailed account books, receipts and accounting vouchers, lists of share purchasers and performance records; the share certificates holding cards of each share-purchasing investor; relevant materials such as the industrial and commercial registrations of Libaidai Company, Nanjing Congtai Investment Management Co., Ltd., and the four involved non-listed joint stock limited companies; as well as the confessions of the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, which were sufficient for determination.

The issues in dispute in this case were: 1. Whether the conduct of the defendant unit Libaidai Company and the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong in this case constituted the crime of illegal business operation; 2. If it constituted the crime of illegal business operation, whether it should be deemed a unit crime.

The Ningbo Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

1. According to the facts of this case, the conduct of the defendant unit Libaidai Company and the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong had already constituted the crime of illegal business operation and should be punished according to law.

First, the conduct of the defendant unit Libaidai Company and the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong violated China's laws, regulations, and policies on the administration of the securities market.

China's securities market implements a securities business licensing system. The public offering of securities must meet the conditions prescribed by laws and administrative regulations and must be approved by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council or the department authorized by the State Council in accordance with the law. Without approval, no unit or individual may publicly offer securities. The General Office of the State Council and the China Securities Regulatory Commission have repeatedly explicitly required severe crackdowns on illegal and criminal activities under the guise of securities and futures investment, and that conduct exceeding the approved business scope, illegally engaging in or disguisedly illegally engaging in securities and futures trading activities, shall be investigated and prosecuted on suspicion of the crime of illegal business operation. The CSRC has explicitly stipulated in a document that illegal activities such as charging agency fees by using the pretext that non-listed companies will be listed and offer high returns from original shares, or fabricating false company performance and promising generous investment returns to induce investors to purchase shares of non-listed companies, constitute illegal agency buying and selling of shares of non-listed companies. The illegal issuance of shares and illegal securities business seriously endanger social stability and financial security. The main forms include: first, fabricating false information that the company will be listed domestically or abroad or that the share issuance has obtained government approval, to induce the public to purchase so-called "original shares"; second, illegal intermediary agencies, in the name of "investment consulting institutions," "property rights brokerage companies," or "representative offices of foreign capital companies or investment companies in China," illegally buying or selling or acting as agents for buying and selling shares of unlisted companies to the public without approval from the competent authorities; third, criminals using securities investment as a pretext and high returns as bait to defraud the public of their money.

In this case, the defendant unit Libaidai Company did not obtain a securities business license issued by the securities regulatory authority of the State Council or the department authorized by the State Council, but without authorization, it publicly acted as an agent to sell shares of non-listed joint stock limited companies to unspecified members of the public, and did so in fragmented offerings. In its business activities, the company falsely claimed that the involved non-listed joint stock limited companies would be listed and that investors could obtain high original share returns, inducing investors to purchase shares of the involved non-listed joint stock limited companies, and charged agency fees and other expenses. Its conduct constituted the illegal act of illegally acting as an agent for buying and selling shares of non-listed companies. The business scope of Libaidai Company, as approved and registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce, was investment planning and consulting for industrial projects, accounting business consulting, enterprise management consulting, enterprise joint-stock reform, and enterprise restructuring planning and consulting, which did not include securities business. After the company was penalized by the administrative department for industry and commerce for exceeding its business scope, it applied for and obtained approval to add "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" to its business scope. However, according to relevant regulations, "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" refers to service activities where an agent accepts a commission from the property rights owner and submits a property rights transaction application to a property rights transaction institution in the name of the property rights owner, and does not involve other property rights transaction marketing activities. According to relevant regulations, a property rights transaction brokerage institution refers to an intermediary institution with the professional qualification for property rights transactions that accepts a commission from an enterprise to act as an agent for property rights transactions, and personnel engaged in property rights transaction business must have corresponding brokerage qualifications. Libaidai Company did not have the professional qualification for property rights transactions and was not a property rights transaction brokerage institution. The defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, Zheng Chunzhong, and other personnel of Libaidai Company also did not have corresponding brokerage qualifications. Libaidai Company exceeded the business scope approved and registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce, was neither authorized nor licensed to engage in securities business, and did not have the qualification of a property rights transaction brokerage institution, yet illegally engaged in securities trading activities. Its conduct constituted illegal business operation.

Second, the conduct of the defendant unit Libaidai Company and the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong constituted the crime of illegal business operation.

According to Article 225 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Criminal Law"), the crime of illegal business operation refers to illegal business conduct that severely disrupts market order and has serious circumstances, such as operating without a license for goods that are monopolized or restricted from sale under laws and administrative regulations, buying or selling import and export licenses, certificates of origin, and other business licenses or approval documents required by laws and administrative regulations. As discussed above, the conduct of the defendant unit Libaidai Company and the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong in this case constituted illegal business operation. The defendant unit and the three defendants acted as agents for the sale of shares of four non-listed joint stock limited companies to a total of 216 persons, selling a total of 1,888,500 shares of non-listed joint stock limited companies, with a total sales amount exceeding RMB 6.57 million, and illegally profited more than RMB 2.4 million. In terms of consequences, whether the shares of the involved non-listed joint stock limited companies purchased by the involved share-purchasing investors could ultimately be recognized by the involved non-listed joint stock limited companies was highly problematic, and they were very likely just worthless paper. It could be determined that the illegal business operation of the defendant unit and the three defendants had serious circumstances, a wide scope of harm, and significant social harm, and had already constituted the crime of illegal business operation, for which criminal liability should be pursued according to law.

2. This case did not constitute a unit crime.

According to the facts of this case, the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong, for the purpose of illegally engaging in the agency sale of shares of non-listed joint stock limited companies, registered and established the defendant unit Libaidai Company. After its establishment, Libaidai Company engaged in no other business activities other than the illegal operation crime involved. According to Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Unit Crime Cases, where a company, enterprise, or institution established by an individual for the purpose of engaging in illegal and criminal activities commits a crime, or where a company, enterprise, or institution, after its establishment, primarily engages in criminal activities, it shall not be treated as a unit crime. Therefore, the three defendants established Libaidai Company for the purpose of illegally engaging in securities business, and after its establishment, Libaidai Company primarily engaged in illegal securities business activities. Accordingly, this case could not be treated as a unit crime but should be deemed a natural person crime.

In summary, the defendants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong established the defendant unit Libaidai Company for the purpose of illegally engaging in securities business. In their operations, they exceeded the business scope approved and registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce and, without approval from the competent authorities, without authorization openly acted as agents to transfer equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies to unspecified members of the public. After being penalized by the administrative department for industry and commerce for exceeding the business scope, they continued to exceed the business scope by illegally engaging in securities business under the pretext of adding "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" to their business scope. Even after the relevant administrative law enforcement departments pointed out that they were not authorized to engage in securities business, they still did not cease the illegal activities, disrupting the national securities market. The circumstances were serious, and their conduct had all constituted the crime of illegal business operation. The charges in the indictment were established. The defenses of the three defendants and their defense counsels were not established and were not adopted. The three defendants established Libaidai Company for the purpose of illegally engaging in securities business, and after its establishment, Libaidai Company only engaged in illegal business activities. Therefore, this case could not be treated as a unit crime but should be deemed a joint crime by natural persons. The indictment's charge of unit crime was not established and should be corrected. Zheng Chunzhong played a relatively minor role in the joint crime, so a lighter punishment could be imposed on him at the court's discretion. Accordingly, the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 225, Item (3), Article 25, Paragraph 1, and Article 64 of the Criminal Law, rendered the following judgment on February 8, 2007:

1. The defendant Chen Zongwei was convicted of the crime of illegal business operation and sentenced to five years and six months' imprisonment, and fined RMB 2.5 million;
2. The defendant Wang Wenze was convicted of the crime of illegal business operation and sentenced to five years and six months' imprisonment, and fined RMB 2.5 million;
3. The defendant Zheng Chunzhong was convicted of the crime of illegal business operation and sentenced to five years' imprisonment, and fined RMB 2.5 million.
4. The illegal gains from the crime shall be continued to be recovered.

Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong all appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Zhejiang High People's Court. Their main grounds of appeal were: The three appellants, in operating Libaidai Company, engaged in agency transfer business of property rights (equity) within the business scope of "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" approved by the administrative department for industry and commerce, and thus did not exceed the business scope; the agency transfer of equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies did not constitute engaging in securities business; the original trial's finding that the three appellants did not cease the illegal business operation after being explicitly informed by the relevant administrative law enforcement departments that they were not authorized to operate was not based on facts; the three appellants did not have the criminal intent for illegal business operation. Accordingly, they requested a verdict of not guilty. Zheng Chunzhong and his defense counsel further appealed that Zheng Chunzhong was merely an employee of Libaidai Company and played only a secondary or auxiliary role in the involved equity transfer business. Wang Wenze further appealed that the administrative department for industry and commerce's approval for Libaidai Company to add "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" to its business scope gave rise to his reasonable reliance, and he did not have the criminal intent for illegal business operation.

Upon second instance, the Zhejiang High People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Zhejiang High People's Court held at second instance:

China's securities market implements a securities business licensing system. Without approval from the securities regulatory authority of the State Council or the department authorized by the State Council, no person may engage in securities business. The appellants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong established Libaidai Company and, without approval from the competent authorities, without authorization accepted commissions to transfer equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies to unspecified members of the public, and did so in fragmented transfers, which constituted illegal securities business. Their conduct had already constituted the crime of illegal business operation. The appellants and their defense counsels' ground of appeal that the agency transfer of equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies did not constitute engaging in securities business could not be established and was not adopted. After the establishment of Libaidai Company, the three appellants engaged in the agency transfer of equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies, which clearly exceeded the business scope approved and registered by the administrative department for industry and commerce. After being penalized for exceeding the business scope, the company applied to add "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" to its business scope. However, this business only refers to accepting a commission from the property rights owner to submit a property rights transaction application to a property rights transaction institution in the name of the property rights owner, and does not include the agency transfer of equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies. According to the explanations given by Shi Minwei, Hu Jian, and Fan Zhihua of the Ningbo Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, and Zheng Kangbin of the Ningbo Regulatory Bureau of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, which were presented and cross-examined at the first-instance trial, at a coordination meeting held in May 2004, the relevant administrative law enforcement departments pointed out to the three appellants that: After Libaidai Company added "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures" to its business scope, engaging in the agency transfer of equity of non-listed joint stock limited companies still exceeded the business scope, and to engage in such business, approval from the relevant securities regulatory authority was required. However, thereafter, the three appellants continued to engage in such business. Accordingly, it could be determined that the three appellants had the criminal intent for illegal business operation. The appellants and their defense counsels' grounds of appeal that the original trial's finding that the three appellants did not cease the illegal business operation after being explicitly informed by the relevant administrative law enforcement departments that they were not authorized to engage in securities business was without evidence, that Libaidai Company did not exceed its business scope after adding "handling applications for property rights transaction procedures," and that they did not have the criminal intent for illegal business operation, could not be established and were not adopted. As Deputy General Manager of Libaidai Company, Zheng Chunzhong's status and role in the joint crime were relatively secondary compared to Chen Zongwei and Wang Wenze, but he did not obviously play a secondary or auxiliary role and was not an accomplice. The first instance had already imposed a lighter punishment on him at its discretion. Zheng Chunzhong and his defense counsel's ground of appeal that Zheng Chunzhong played only a secondary or auxiliary role in the joint crime could not be established and was not adopted.

Accordingly, the Zhejiang High People's Court held that the first instance judgment had clearly found the facts, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the application of law was correct, the conviction and sentencing were appropriate, and the trial procedures were lawful. The grounds of appeal raised by the appellants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, Zheng Chunzhong, and their defense counsels were all untenable. In accordance with Article 189, Paragraph (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Court ruled on June 14, 2007 as follows:

The appeals of the appellants Chen Zongwei, Wang Wenze, and Zheng Chunzhong are dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
